sections.h2: What does the Mason County Register of Deeds office do?
sections.html:
The Mason County Register of Deeds keeps the official record of every deed, mortgage and other instrument that conveys or encumbers land in the county. Michigan's constitution makes the register an elected county officer on a four-year partisan term. Under MCL 565.551 the office must provide reasonable facilities for anyone to inspect and examine its records.

The register also chairs the county plat board, which reviews proposed subdivision plats before they go to the state. The other seats on that board belong to the county clerk and the county treasurer.

The office lists three sets of hours, all Monday through Friday except legal holidays:

  • Business hours: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Recording hours: 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Passport applications: 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Ask the Mason County office for its street address and direct phone line before you send documents.

sections.h2: What should a Mason County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Mason County has Ludington as its seat and largest city, and it was created in 1840 under the name Notipekago before taking its present name in 1843. Of its 1,242 square miles, 495 are land and 60 percent is water. US 10 runs east to west through the middle of the county, US 31 comes in from the south and meets it near Ludington, and M-116 follows the Lake Michigan shore to Ludington State Park. Part of the Manistee National Forest lies inside the county.

The Census Bureau estimated 29,040 people for July 1, 2025. QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 give the following housing picture:

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $219,600
  • Owner-occupied rate: 78.3 percent
  • Median gross rent: $896
  • Residents aged 65 or older: 28.8 percent
  • Median household income: $64,748

Families passing a house to a child or grandchild should note that MCL 207.526 exempts those deeds from state transfer tax, and the exemption has to be written on the deed.

sections.h2: How much does the Mason County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Mason County charges $30.00 for each deed, mortgage, lis pendens or other instrument. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for every extra instrument. Copies run $1.00 per page, plat copies $2.00 per page, and certifying a copy costs $5.00.

A records search by name costs 50 cents per year searched, with a $5.00 minimum. State and federal tax lien certificate searches are $3.00 per name. The county's fee page was last updated in February 2018, so confirm the figures with the office before you send a check.

Document images and indexes from June 23, 1840 forward are online. Frequent users can choose a prepaid subscription plan, and occasional users can pay by card per search. The county says the online index is a working index that can contain errors and is not a certification.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Mason County sale?
sections.html:
Transfer tax in Mason County is $4.30 for each $500 of price or fraction of $500, made up of $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county. The seller owes it, and it is due on any deed given for $100 or more.

Mason County transfer tax at three sale prices, taken from the county's tax table
Sale price up toStateCountyTotal
$50,000$375.00$55.00$430.00
$75,000$562.50$82.50$645.00
$100,000$750.00$110.00$860.00

Past $100,000 the same arithmetic continues. A $200,000 sale is 400 steps of $500, so $1,720 in combined tax, and a $250,000 sale comes to $2,150. The county's table is the place to check a price that falls between the rows.

The county lists separate exemption pages for its share and the state's share, and any exemption claimed must be written on the document. MCL 207.526 exempts, among others, deeds from a parent or grandparent to a child or grandchild, transfers in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure, and land contracts where title has not yet passed.

sections.h2: What does Michigan require on a deed before Mason County records it?
sections.html:
The register of deeds posts the text of MCL 565.201 as its recording requirements. A deed signed after April 1, 1997 must show each signer's printed name under the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and the notary's printed name on the same page. Every grantee's address and the drafter's name and business address belong on the instrument.

The page layout also matters:

  • A 2 1/2 inch unprinted top margin on page one, and 1/2 inch margins elsewhere
  • 10-point type or larger, in black ink on white paper of at least 20-pound weight
  • Sheets between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches
  • A first line that names one recordable event only
  • An English translation attached to anything written in another language
  • The first five digits of a Social Security number removed

Once the register accepts and records an instrument, the statute treats it as conforming. That is why a closing agent usually reviews the deed before it is presented.

sections.h2: Who certifies the taxes on a Mason County deed?
sections.html:
The Mason County Treasurer. The treasurer's page says the office certifies deeds before recording to show no delinquent taxes for the five years before the date of the instrument, and it also issues tax abstracts and histories. A warranty deed, land contract, assignment of a land contract or deed with a covenant of warranty needs this certificate (MCL 211.135).

The treasurer's office is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and its property tax line is 231 843-8411. Real property taxes become delinquent on March 1, when the township and city rolls pass to the county treasurer at settlement. Village taxes are the exception to that March 1 rule.

Mason County has been an opt-in county for tax foreclosure since 2004, so the county treasurer, not the state, runs the foreclosure and sale of tax-delinquent parcels. It is also an opt-in county for principal residence exemption audits. Audits of exemptions claimed in error therefore come from the county treasurer's office.

sections.h2: Which Mason County office handles parcel splits and address changes?
sections.html:
The Equalization Department, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday at 231-845-6288. It assigns addresses for every unit except Ludington and Scottville, and it processes parcel splits and combinations, mailing address updates and tax map requests. It also hosts the county parcel GIS layer, the apportionment report and the annual equalization report.

This matters in a sale when a buyer wants only part of a lot or a lakeside parcel is being divided. The register of deeds records the deed, and equalization then updates the parcel records.

The register of deeds also offers Mason County property owners a free Property Fraud Alert service, with sign-up details on the office's page.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee in Mason County?
faqs.a: It is $30.00 per document. A document that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra one. Copies are $1.00 per page and certification is $5.00.

faqs.q: What are the Mason County Register of Deeds recording hours?
faqs.a: Recording runs 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday except legal holidays. General business hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Documents arriving after 4:30 p.m. may wait for the next business day, so plan closings accordingly.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I pay on a $200,000 sale in Mason County?
faqs.a: About $1,720 combined, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county. The seller owes it unless the deed qualifies for an exemption. Exemptions must be stated on the document.

faqs.q: Does Mason County require a tax certificate for a deed?
faqs.a: Yes, for warranty deeds and land contracts. The county treasurer certifies that no taxes are delinquent for the previous five years. Quitclaim deeds without a covenant of warranty are excused under MCL 211.135.

faqs.q: How far back do Mason County online land records go?
faqs.a: Document images and indexes are online from June 23, 1840 to the present. The county notes that the index is a working index, so confirm important details against the recorded document itself.
